newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's J.Martins ponders Vidago bid.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's J.Martins ponders Vidago bid.

text.p: Portuguese retailer Jeronimo Martins said it was studying the possibility of making a public offer (OPA) to buy all the shares of mineral water group Vidago and that no decision had been taken as to whether to bid.
"The board of Jeronimo Martins is studying the possibility of launching an OPA for the shares of Vidago, Melgaco e Pedras Salgadas SA, but has taken no definitive decision," a statement said.
Earlier, Jeronimo Martins, Portugal's second biggest retailer, said it posted a 48 percent hike in nine-month profit to 7.3 billion escudos ($48 million).

It said the contribution from a chain of cash-and-carry shops in Poland and the rapid expansion of the Lillywhites sports goods group had a positive impact on its profit, sharply up from 4.9 billion escudos in the same year-ago period.
"These results reflect the fulfilment of the profit potential from the acquisitions," a statement said.

Jeronimo Martins's shares were suspended on the Lisbon bourse on Thursday morning because the company had released no statement after Diario de Noticias newspaper reported it had bought Vidago on Wednesday for 15.5 billion escudos ($102 million).
Vidago said in a statement on Thursday that some shareholders were studying the possibility of selling their holdings but that it was unaware of any plans for a third party to bid for it.
The board was unaware of any reason for a sharp appreciation in the value of the company's stock, it said.
Vidago shares were suspended on Monday as rumours swirled of a takeover bid.
